item.title: Representation Theory and the Algebraic K-Theory of Geometric Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.15605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply a derived completion construction for commutative ring spectra to give a description of the K-theory spectrum of a geometric field F (i.e. containing an algebraically closed subfield $k$) of characteristic zero purely in terms of the representation theory of its absolute Galois group $G_F$. A result that follows is that the l-adically completed Milnor K-theory of F is isomorphic to the derived completion of the representation ring of $G_F$. The main result, from which this follows, is that $K(F)$ completed at l is equivalent to the derived completion of the K-theory of the category of finite dimensional representations of $G_F$ in $k$.
item.dc:creator: Gunnar Carlsson, Roy Joshua

item.title: Bloch groups of local rings with residue field $\mathbb{F}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a generic presentation of the pre-Bloch group of a local ring with residue field $\mathbb{F}_{2}$. We apply this to the calculation of pre-Bloch groups and Bloch groups of some local rings.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Hutchinson

item.title: Immaculate complexes and Strong Generation by Injectives
item.description: arXiv:2611.16680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the category of bounded complexes of finite sums of indecomposable injectives over a locally Noetherian scheme, which we call the immaculate complexes. We show that regularity and finiteness of dimension can be detected from this category using strong generation. Our methods involve studying when the unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck category is strongly generated by injectives. As applications we prove a conjecture of Hartshorne and recover a result of Keller and Krause. To any specialisation closed subset we associate a semi-orthogonal decomposition of the immaculates and use this to compute additive finitary invariants in terms of the completions of the local rings. The immaculates are equivalent to the perfect derived category of a left coherent preadditive category i.e. a ring with many objects and we compute this category for one-dimensional integral or Gorenstein schemes.
item.dc:creator: Isambard Goodbody

item.title: Remarks on refined scissors congruence group and the third homology of $\mathrm{SL}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2608.08890v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work revisits the key sufficient conditions on a ring $A$ that guarantee the existence of the exact sequence \[ H_3(\mathrm{SM}_2(A), \mathbb{Z})\to H_3(\mathrm{SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z}) \to \mathcal{RB}(A) \to 0 \] and of the isomorphism \[ H_3(\mathrm{SL}_2(A), \mathrm{SM}_2(A); \mathbb{Z}) \simeq \mathcal{RP}_1(A). \] We show that there are rings which satisfy the relations above but do not satisfy the condition that -1 is an square, for example some rings $\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1}{m}]$ and finite local rings. In addition, we study the special case of non-dyadic local fields with characteristic not 2, obtaining a refined Bloch-Wigner exact sequence when -1 is not an square.
item.dc:creator: Elvis Torres P\'erez

item.title: The Gromov-Lawson-Rosenberg Conjecture for Z/4xZ/4
item.description: arXiv:2408.07895v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the Gromov-Lawson-Rosenberg Conjecture for the group Z/4xZ/4 by computing the connective real k-homology of the classifying space with the Adams spectral sequence and two types of detection theorems for the kernel of the alpha invariant: one based on eta-invariants, closely following work of Botvinnik-Gilkey-Stolz, and a second one based on homological methods. Along the way, we determine differentials of the Adams spectral sequence for classifying spaces involved in the computation, and we study the cap structure of the Adams spectral sequence for sub-hopf algebras of the Steenrod algebra relevant to the computation of connective real and complex k-homology.
item.dc:creator: Noe Barcenas, Luis Eduardo Garcia-Hernandez, Raphael Reinauer

item.title: Leafwise positive scalar curvature and the Rosenberg index
item.description: arXiv:2502.02325v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a closed spin manifold, in this paper, we show that if there is a foliation $(M,F)$ and a Riemannian metric on $M$ that has leafwise positive scalar curvature then the Rosenberg index of $M$ is zero.
item.dc:creator: Guangxiang Su, Zelin Yi

item.title: A full-rank subgroup of Bloch Groups of CM Fields
item.description: arXiv:2507.05792v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article generalizes the result of Burns et al (2022), to find an algorithm to find some elements generating a full-rank subgroup of the torsion-free part of Bloch group of a certain CM number field, and compute the rank of it.
item.dc:creator: Wenhuan Huang

item.title: The Simplicial Cylinder DG Ring
item.description: arXiv:2602.11943v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Keller cylinder DG ring encodes homotopies between DG ring homomorphisms $f_0, f_1 : A \to B$. Recently we discovered the higher cylinder DG rings $Cyl_q(B)$, which assemble into the simplicial cylinder DG ring $Cyl(B)$. For $q=1$ this recovers Keller's original construction. The sets $SHom_q(A,B)$ of DG ring homomorphisms $A \to Cyl_q(B)$ form the simplicial Hom set $SHom(A,B)$. Our main result is that when $A$ is a semi-free DG ring, the simplicial set $SHom(A,B)$ is a Kan complex. We prove several results about the fundamental groupoid $SHom_{\leq 1}(A,B)$, including invariance under quasi-isomorphism $B' \to B$.
item.dc:creator: Amnon Yekutieli
